lines.text: In nineteen eighty-five, Costco introduced a hot dog for one dollar and fifty cents.
Four decades later, that price has never changed.
Today, it loses forty million dollars every single year.
When an executive wanted to raise it, the founder gave a blunt warning.
If you raise that hot dog, I will kill you.
Why defend a cheap meal so fiercely?
Because it is retail's greatest loss leader.
Nobody leaves with just a hot dog.
Shoppers fill huge carts, then pay sixty dollars to renew their membership.
That dollar-fifty meal quietly anchored a three hundred billion dollar empire.
